limits.short: These are annual figures that utilities reported to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. They are not live outage data, and utilities may calculate them in different ways.

metric.noObservations: No observations are available for this metric and selection.
metric.single: Only one reported year is available; a change over time cannot be assessed.
metric.discrepancyYears: Years with duplicate or invalid observations (not plotted)
metric.meaning: These are historical system averages, not an individual household’s outage experience or a prediction of its next outage. Reliability figures alone do not establish weather-related causes. Backup-power scenarios are separate, hypothetical household choices.
metric.tableNote: Not reported means missing, never zero. Entirely empty other-standard rows are hidden; customer-count-only rows remain visible. Source records are unchanged.
chart.legend: Bars show reported values. A dot on the baseline means a reported zero. A dash (-) marks a missing observation; no bar is drawn. An exclamation mark (!) indicates a reporting discrepancy. Exact values are in the yearly table below.
metric.saidiMeaning: SAIDI describes total reported interruption minutes averaged across customers over the year.
metric.saifiMeaning: SAIFI describes the reported number of sustained interruptions averaged across customers over the year. A fractional value is a system average.
metric.caidiMeaning: CAIDI describes average duration per reported customer interruption. It is not a household’s total annual outage time. Missing CAIDI is not calculated from rounded SAIDI and SAIFI.
metric.scales: Each chart uses its own vertical scale. Compare years within a chart; bar heights across different metrics are not comparable.
